question.text: In a hardware store, there are three boxes containing light bulbs. Box $A$ contains $15$ bulbs, of which $2$ are defective. Box $B$ contains $10$ bulbs, of which $1$ is defective. And box $C$ contains $10$ light bulbs, of which $2$ are defective. A box is selected at random, and a bulb is randomly selected from the box. Find the probability that the bulb is defective.
question.explanation:
Let $D$ be the event of selecting a defective bulb, and

  • let $A$ be the event that the bulb is from box $A,$

  • let $B$ be the event that the bulb is from box $B$

  • let $C$ be the event that the bulb is from box $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a defective bulb at random from one of the three boxes, we can use the law of total probability:

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D \cap A) + P(D \cap B) + P(D \cap C) \\[5pt] &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \end{align*}

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a box is selected at random, we have \[ P(A) = P(B) = P(C) = \dfrac{1}{3}. \]

  • Since there are $2$ defective bulbs out of $15$ in box $A, $ $1$ defective bulb out of $10$ in box $B,$ and $2$ defective bulbs out of $10$ bulbs in box $C,$ we have \[ P(D |A ) = \dfrac{2}{15}, \qquad P(D | B) = \dfrac{1}{10}, \qquad P(D | C) = \dfrac{2}{10}. \]

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a defective bulb at random from one of the three boxes is

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \\[5pt] &= \left( \dfrac{2}{15} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{10} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right)+ \left( \dfrac{2}{10} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2}{45} + \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{2}{30} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{13}{90}. \end{align*}

question.text: A company produces replacement batteries for a particular cell phone model at three locations. Location $A$ produces $30\%$ of the batteries, of which $3\%$ are defective. Location $B$ produces $38\%$ of the batteries, of which $5\%$ are defective. And location $C$ produces $ 32\%$ of the batteries, of which also $5\%$ are defective. What is the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective?
question.explanation:
Let $D$ be the event that the battery is defective, and

  • let $A$ be the event that the battery was produced at location $A,$

  • let $B$ be the event that the battery was produced at location $B,$

  • let $C$ be the event that the battery was produced at location $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D \cap A) + P(D \cap B) + P(D \cap C) \\[5pt] &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \end{align*}

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since location $A$ produces $30\%$ of the batteries, location $B$ produces $38 \%$ of the batteries, and location $C$ produces $32 \%$ of the batteries, we have \[ P(A) = 0.3, \qquad P(B) = 0.38, \qquad P(C)=0.32. \]

  • Since $3\%$ of the batteries produced at location $A$, $5\%$ of the batteries produced at location $B$, and $5\%$ of the batteries produced at location $C,$ are defective, we have \[ P(D | A) = 0.03, \qquad P(D | B) = 0.05, \qquad P(D | C) = 0.05. \]

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected battery is defective is

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \\[5pt] &= \left( 0.03 \right) \left(0.3 \right) + \left( 0.05 \right) \left( 0.38 \right) + \left( 0.05 \right) \left( 0.32 \right) \\[5pt] &= 0.009 + 0.019 + 0.016 \\[5pt] &= 0.044. \end{align*}

question.text: In a gas station, $40\%$ of the clients buy Regular gasoline, $45\%$ buy Premium gasoline, and $15\%$ buy Supreme gasoline. If $65\%$ of the clients that purchase Regular gasoline paid with a credit card, $50\%$ of the clients that buy Premium gasoline paid with a credit card, and $60\%$ of the clients that buy Supreme gasoline paid with a credit card, what is the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card?
question.explanation:
Let $C$ be the event that the client paid with a credit card, and

  • let $R$ be the event that the client bought Regular gasoline,

  • let $Q$ be the event that the client bought Premium gasoline,

  • let $S$ be the event that the client bought Supreme gasoline.

Then the disjoint union $R \sqcup Q \sqcup S$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card, we can use the law of total probability:

\begin{align*} P(C) &= P(C \cap R) + P(C \cap Q) + P(C \cap S) \\[5pt] &= P(C | R) P(R) + P(C | Q) P(Q) + P(C | S) P(S) \end{align*}

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since $40\%$ of the clients buy Regular gasoline, $45\%$ of the clients buy Premium gasoline, and $15\%$ of the clients buy Supreme gasoline, we have \[ P(R) = 0.4, \qquad P(Q) = 0.45, \qquad P(S) = 0.15. \]

  • Since $65\%$ of the clients that buy Regular gasoline, $50\%$ of the clients that buy Premium gasoline, and $60\%$ of the clients that buy Supreme gasoline, paid with a credit card, we have \[ P(C | R) = 0.65, \qquad P(C | Q) = 0.5, \qquad P(C | S) = 0.6. \]

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected client paid with a credit card is

\begin{align*} P(C) &= P(C | R) P(R) + P(C | Q) P(Q) + P(C | S) P(S)\\[5pt] &= \left( 0.65 \right) \left(0.4 \right) + \left( 0.5 \right) \left( 0.45 \right) + \left( 0.6 \right) \left( 0.15 \right) \\[5pt] &= 0.26 + 0.225 + 0.009 \\[5pt] &= 0.575. \end{align*}

question.text: A company manufactures electronic components. Of the component population, $45\%$ are produced by machine $A,$ $25\% $ by machine $B,$ and $30 \%$ by machine $C.$ If $5 \%$ of the components produced by machine $A$ and $3 \%$ of those produced by machine $B$ are defective, and the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is $0.042,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected component produced by machine $C$ is defective?
question.explanation:
Let $D$ be the event that a randomly selected component is defective, and

  • let $A$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $A,$

  • let $B$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $B,$

  • let $C$ be the event that the component was produced by machine $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected component is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D \cap A) + P(D \cap B) + P(D \cap C) \\[5pt] &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \end{align*}

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since machine $A$ produces $45\%$ of the components, machine $B$ produces $25\%$ of the components, and machine $C $ produces $30\%$ of the components, we have \[ P(A) = 0.45, \qquad P(B) = 0.25, \qquad P(C)=0.3. \]

  • Since $5\%$ of the components produced by machine $A$ and $3\%$ of the components produced by machine $B$ are defective, we have \[ P(D|A) = 0.05, \qquad P(D|B) = 0.03 \]

  • Since the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is $0.042,$ we have \[ P(D) = 0.042. \]

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(D|C),$ we get

\[\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C)\\[5pt] 0.042 &= \left( 0.05 \right) \left( 0.45 \right) + \left( 0.03 \right) \left( 0.25 \right) + P(D|C) \left( 0.3 \right) \\[5pt] 0.042 &= 0.0225 + 0.0075 + 0.3P(D|C) \\[5pt] 0.3P(D|C) &= 0.012 \\[5pt] P(D|C) &= 0.04 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected component produced by machine $C$ is defective is $0.04.$

question.text: A cattle rancher has three ranches, where $34\%$ of the rancher's cows are on ranch $A$, $36\%$ are on ranch $B,$ and $30\%$ on ranch $C.$ If $25\%$ of all cows on ranch $A$ and $20\%$ of all cows on ranch $B$ are dairy cows, and the probability that a randomly selected cow from any of the three ranches is a dairy cow is $37\%,$ what is the probability that a randomly selected cow from ranch $C$ is a dairy cow?
question.explanation:
Let $D$ be the event that a selected cow is a dairy cow, and

  • let $A$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $A$,

  • let $B$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $B$,

  • let $C$ be the event that the cow is from ranch $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that the randomly selected cow is a dairy cow, we use the law of total probability:

\begin{align*} P(D) &= P(D \cap A) + P(D \cap B) + P(D \cap C) \\[5pt] &= P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \end{align*}

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since $34\%$ of all the rancher's cows are on ranch $A$, $36\%$ are on ranch $B,$ and $30\%$ are on ranch $C,$ we have
    \[ P(A) = 0.34, \quad P(B) =0.36, \quad P(C) = 0.3. \]

  • Since $25\%$ of all cows on ranch $A$ and $20\%$ of all cows on ranch $B$ are dairy cows, we have \[ P(D |A ) = 0.25, \qquad P(D | B) = 0.2. \]

  • Since the probability that a randomly selected cow from any of the three ranches is a dairy cow is $37\%,$ we have \[ P(D) = 0.37. \]

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(D|C),$ we get

\[\begin{align*} P(D) &=P(D | A) P(A) + P(D | B) P(B) + P(D | C) P(C) \\[5pt] 0.37&= \left( 0.25 \right) \left( 0.34\right ) + \left(0.2 \right) \left( 0.36\right) + P(D|C) \left( 0.3\right) \\[5pt] 0.37 &= 0.085 + 0.072+ 0.3P(D|C) \\[5pt] 0.3P(D|C) &=0.213\\[5pt] P(D|C) &= 0.71 \end{align*}\]

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected cow from ranch $C$ is a dairy cow is $71\%. $
